title: CHAIN-OF-VERIFICATION REDUCES HALLUCINATION IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
abstract: This paper introduces the Chain-of-Verification (CoVe) method, which reduces hallucination in large language models by having the model deliberate on its responses and correct its mistakes.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're having a conversation with a large language model. You ask it a question, and it responds with a plausible but incorrect answer. This is called hallucination. The CoVe method helps the model correct its mistakes by planning verification questions and answering them independently.

This approach is like a fact-checking process, where the model verifies its own responses to ensure accuracy.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
The CoVe method works by first generating a baseline response to a given question. Then, it plans verification questions to check the factual claims in the response. These questions are answered independently, and the results are used to generate a final verified response.

This process helps to reduce hallucination and improve the accuracy of the model's responses.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
The CoVe method was evaluated on several benchmark tasks, including Wikidata, Wiki-Category list, and MultiSpanQA. The results show that CoVe improves precision and reduces hallucination compared to the baseline model.

For example, on the Wikidata task, CoVe achieved a precision of 0.36, outperforming the baseline model's precision of 0.17.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The CoVe method has significant implications for improving the accuracy and reliability of large language models. By reducing hallucination, CoVe can help models provide more trustworthy responses, which is essential for applications such as question answering and text generation.

Additionally, CoVe can be used to improve the performance of models on a wide range of tasks, from simple question answering to complex text generation.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
The CoVe method introduces several key innovations, including the use of verification questions to check the factual claims in a response, and the use of independent answering to reduce hallucination.

Additionally, CoVe uses a factored approach to separate the verification questions from the original response, which helps to improve performance and reduce hallucination.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try out the CoVe method, you can use a large language model such as Llama 65B and provide it with a few-shot prompt that includes demonstrations of verification questions and final verified responses.

You can then evaluate the performance of the model on a benchmark task, such as Wikidata or MultiSpanQA, and compare the results to the baseline model.
